title: Pasta alla zozzona
subtitle: Roman pasta with sausage, guanciale, tomato, and egg
excerpt: Pasta alla zozzona is a Roman 'everything in the pan' pasta: guanciale, pork sausage, tomato, and egg yolk, combined into one rich sauce. The name means 'dirty' or 'slovenly' in Roman dialect, a joke about how indulgent the combination is. It is, in the best possible way, a very generous pasta.
sourceNotes: Roman trattoria recipe. The zozzona is considered an unofficial 'fifth Roman pasta', combining elements of carbonara (egg, guanciale, pecorino) with amatriciana (tomato) and adding sausage. Widely documented in Roman food writing from the 2000s onwards.

content.text: Pasta alla zozzona combines the best bits of three Roman pastas (carbonara, amatriciana, and gricia) and then adds pork sausage on top.

content.text: Put the guanciale in a cold, wide frying pan and set over medium heat. Render until the fat is translucent and the batons are lightly golden, about 6 minutes. Crumble in the sausagemeat and cook, breaking it up, for 5 minutes until brown. Pour off excess fat, leaving 2 tablespoons.
Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} of crushed tomatoes. Season with black pepper. Simmer for 15 minutes until the sauce has thickened.
Cook the pasta and add the egg
Cook {{pasta-dried}} of rigatoni in a large pot of salted boiling water until 2 minutes short of al dente. Reserve a large mug of pasta water, then drain.
Whisk the {{egg-yolks}} of egg yolks with the Pecorino and a little black pepper in a small bowl. Add 3 tablespoons of hot pasta water to the yolks and whisk quickly to temper them.

Add the pasta to the tomato-meat sauce. Remove from the heat. Pour the egg mixture over and toss continuously, adding pasta water a little at a time, until the sauce is thick and glossy. Serve immediately.

items.cause: Pan was too hot when the yolks were added.
items.fix: Always remove the pan from the heat before adding the egg mixture. Toss quickly and add pasta water to cool the sauce.

items.cause: Too much egg-yolk to pasta water ratio.
items.fix: Loosen with more pasta water a tablespoon at a time.

items.cause: Not enough fat rendered off before adding the sausage.
items.fix: Let the guanciale render for the full 6 minutes, and drain off excess fat before adding the tomato.

content.text: The zozzona is the informal, trattoria side of Roman cooking: food served in old-school restaurants that care more about flavour than elegance. It is younger than the four main Roman pastas (carbonara, amatriciana, cacio e pepe, and gricia) but has built a loyal following in Rome's local osterie. The name is proudly brash, which is part of the point.
